SMCI or NTAP: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?

SMCI

Trading disclosure

Investors with an interest in Computer- Storage Devices stocks have likely encountered both Super Micro Computer (SMCI) and NetApp (NTAP). But which of these two stocks offers value investors a better bang for their buck right now? We'll need to take a closer look.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The Zacks Rank favors stocks with strong earnings estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight companies with specific traits.

Currently, both Super Micro Computer and NetApp are holding a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy). This system places an emphasis on companies that have seen positive earnings estimate revisions, so investors should feel comfortable knowing that these stocks have improving earnings outlooks. But this is just one piece of the puzzle for value investors.

Value investors are also interested in a number of tried-and-true valuation metrics that help show when a company is undervalued at its current share price levels.

Our Value category highlights undervalued companies by looking at a variety of key metrics, including the popular P/E ratio, as well as the P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a variety of other fundamentals that have been used by value investors for years.

SMCI currently has a forward P/E ratio of 8.44, while NTAP has a forward P/E of 18.27. We also note that SMCI has a PEG ratio of 0.64. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. NTAP currently has a PEG ratio of 1.64.

Another notable valuation metric for SMCI is its P/B ratio of 2.19. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, NTAP has a P/B of 24.12.

Based on these metrics and many more, SMCI holds a Value grade of B, while NTAP has a Value grade of D.

Both SMCI and NTAP are impressive stocks with solid earnings outlooks, but based on these valuation figures, we feel that SMCI is the superior value option right now.

The YieldMax SMCI Option Income Strategy ETF (SMCY, Financials) is an actively managed fund created on exposure to Super Micro Computer, and investors are getting an eye-catching income stream from it. YieldMax shows the fund's distribution rate as 100.90%.That number need some background. SMCY doesn't get that cash via regular dividends. The fund offers call spreads on Super Micro Computer Inc. and collects option premiums off the volatile server maker's share price for weekly payouts.The last dividend was $0.105 per share, announced Sept. 9 and to be paid Sept. 11. So like 98% of the distribution or so was return of capital.This is an important distinction because the distribution rate is not the same as the investment yield. SMCY's 30-day SEC yield was a mere 1.83% as of Aug. 31. But Super Micro has given the approach plenty of instability to work with.AI server provider estimated fiscal 2027 sales of $65 billion to $72 billion, considerably above Wall Street projections, as data-center customers continue spending substantially on artificial intelligence infrastructure.That increase can support interest in SMCI and its option premiums. For investors, SMCY is a compromise. The fund can pay out large weekly cash dividends, but distributions can include returned capital and the options method can limit some upside if Super Micro shares rally.

title: Dear Super Micro Stock Fans, Here's What August's Rally Means for SMCI
detail:
Dear Super Micro Stock Fans, Here's What August's Rally Means for SMCI
Ruchi Gupta
Thu, September 10, 2026 at 8:40 AM PDT 3 min read
SMCI
Trade SMCI on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Supermicro headquarters in San Jose, By JHVEPhoto

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) is a San Jose, California-based provider of high-performance server and storage solutions built on a modular, open-standard architecture. Under founder and CEO Charles Liang, Supermicro designs liquid- and air-cooled AI servers, rack-scale computing platforms, and total Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS) that combine compute, storage, networking, and lifecycle services for AI infrastructure buildouts.

The company has rapidly transformed from a traditional server manufacturer into a comprehensive AI data center solutions provider, serving hyperscalers, enterprises, and cloud service providers worldwide. With manufacturing facilities across the U.S., Taiwan, Malaysia, and the Netherlands, Supermicro remains a critical enabler of the global AI infrastructure boom.

SMCI Posted Mixed Q4 Results

Supermicro's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results showed revenue of $11.1 billion, up 93% year-over-year (YoY) but narrowly missing Wall Street's roughly $11.3 billion estimate. Non-GAAP earnings per share came in at $1.70, obliterating the $0.92 analyst consensus by more than 84%, marking one of Supermicro's largest earnings surprises as an improved product mix and lower inventory reserves drove profitability higher.

For the full fiscal year 2026, Supermicro posted record revenue of $39.1 billion, up 78% from $22.0 billion in fiscal 2025, with non-GAAP EPS climbing 76% to $3.63. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 17.6% in the fourth quarter, up 750 basis points sequentially, while the company received more than $60 billion in new orders during the quarter, pushing its backlog to record levels heading into fiscal 2027. Nine customers each generated over $1 billion in annual revenue, up from four a year earlier.

Management guided fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue to $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.01 to $1.10, and reiterated full-year fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $65 billion to $72 billion. CEO Charles Liang said demand for Supermicro's AI infrastructure solutions has never been stronger, describing the company as transforming into a "one-stop shop" for building AI factories, with management expecting more than 80% of future revenue to be AI-related.

title: Super Micro (SMCI) Up 3.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
detail:
Super Micro (SMCI) Up 3.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue?
Super Micro (SMCI) Up 3.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue? · Zacks

SMCI
^GSPC
SNDK

Trading disclosure

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Super Micro Computer (SMCI). Shares have added about 3.5% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Super Micro due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at the most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for Super Micro Computer, Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

SMCI Q4 Earnings Surpass Expectations, Revenues Rise Y/Y

Super Micro Computer, Inc. reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $1.70 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 68 cents. The bottom line increased 315% year over year.

SMCI generated net sales of $11.12 billion, which increased 93% year over year and 9% sequentially. Revenues also beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.09%. The strong performance reflected continued demand for AI infrastructure, as well as a sharp pickup in enterprise and channel activity.

SMCI Sees Strong AI Demand Despite Customer Readiness Delays

Super Micro Computer's fourth-quarter revenues came in the low end of its previously provided $11-$12.5 billion guided range, primarily due to delays in customer readiness. Management said some deployments were delayed by shortages or readiness issues related to power, cooling and networking, with the related revenues expected to be recognized in subsequent quarters.

The company disclosed more than $60 billion in new orders, driving its order book and backlog to record levels entering fiscal 2027. Management expects more than 80% of future revenues to come from AI-related solutions based on its backlog.

AI solutions accounted for approximately 60% of fourth-quarter revenues compared with more than 80% in the prior quarter, primarily because of the timing of large AI project ramps. Meanwhile, enterprise and channel revenues rose 172% year over year and 98% sequentially to $5.6 billion, accounting for 50% of total revenues.

The company is also broadening its customer base. Super Micro Computer added several hundred enterprise and other customers over the past year, while the number of customers generating more than $1 billion in annual revenues increased to nine in fiscal 2026 from four in fiscal 2025.

Super Micro Computer's Mix Shift Boosts Profitability

SMCI's profitability improved sharply in the fourth quarter as its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 17.6% from 10.1% as posted in the previous quarter.

The past month has been solid for Super Micro Computer (SMCI) shareholders. SMCI stock has jumped about 23% over the past month after the company delivered solid fourth-quarter results and reported a record backlog, continuing to benefit from strong demand for its AI and IT infrastructure solutions. Super Micro's Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue forecast also beat expectations. The outlook indicates that demand for its AI solutions remains strong while the company continues to expand its enterprise customer base.

While SMCI stock has gained notably, there are two compelling reasons that still support its investment case. But one important risk also poses a challenge. Let's take a closer look.

Super Micro's Backlog and AI Demand

Super Micro Computer is well-positioned to deliver strong growth in fiscal 2027 and beyond, driven by AI demand, a solid backlog, and its growing enterprise customer base. The company reported $39.1 billion in fiscal 2026 revenue, representing an increase of 78% year-over-year (YOY). Momentum accelerated in Q4; revenue climbed 93% YOY and 9% sequentially to $11.1 billion. The company also secured more than $60 billion in new orders by the end of Q4, providing significant visibility into future demand and indicating that AI infrastructure spending remains robust.

Supporting SMCI stock's investment case and future growth is the growing contribution from enterprise and channel customers. Revenue from this group reached $5.6 billion in Q4, accounting for roughly 50% of total sales versus 28% in the prior quarter. Segment revenue increased 172% YOY and 98% sequentially, reflecting strong demand for higher-performance computing, storage, and networking infrastructure.

The changing customer mix is beneficial because it reduces Super Micro's reliance on a relatively small number of major data-center customers. While its enterprise revenue surged, OEM appliance and large data-center customers contributed another $5.5 billion during the quarter.

The near-term outlook also points to exceptionally strong momentum. Management's Q1 revenue guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion implies approximately 200% YOY growth at the midpoint and sequential expansion of roughly 35%.
